current.text: Hachimura joined the Clippers this offseason and replaces John Collins as the starting power forward.
The latest projected Clippers starting five includes Hachimura with Darius Garland, Max Strus, Derrick Jones Jr. and Isaiah Jackson. The speaker is not confident about this lineup.
Brandon Ingram is injured, and the Clippers are one of the most injury-hit teams, with Bradley Beal, Jordan Miller and Konan Niederhauser also out.
With Ingram out, Hachimura will have to take more shots.
Experts expect a usage bump and the biggest role of his career. One projects over 30 minutes, over 18% usage, 2 or more threes, about 16 points and 7 rebounds a game.
Experts call him draftable despite disliking him: a Tier 8 small forward and an upside pick around 164 for points and threes.
Experts disagree on whether he is an offensive upgrade over John Collins: one says he could score a bit more, another calls the swap an offensive downgrade.
The Clippers have a good schedule for our fantasy playoffs (4-3-4 games in weeks 19 to 21) and one of the lowest back-to-back totals in the league with 13.
The Clippers are expected to be one of the worst teams. They do not control their own draft pick, so tanking does not help them.
Coach Ty Lue makes odd rotation choices and changes them. This may be a trial season with long rotations and many players tested.

durable.text: He is a very good three-point shooter, over 40% for three straight seasons, but his three-point volume and usage have always been low.
He shoots a good field goal percentage, around 51% to 54% in recent seasons. He is a consistent shooter with a pull-up midrange game.
He gives very little in assists, steals and blocks.
He rarely gets to the free throw line and is not a good free throw shooter.
He is not a good defender and not much of a creator.
Experts see him as a limited fantasy player who shoots threes on low usage and does little else, similar to Harrison Barnes.

note: He is a bubble player for our 144-player draft: Yahoo ranks him 119 at 1 USD, ESPN 154 at 0 USD, and nobody drafted him in our league last season. Take him only as a 1 USD bench flyer. He fits builds that want FG% and threes and has few turnovers (0.7 projected), but he costs you in assists, steals and free throws. Early in the season, check whether he plays over 30 minutes and shoots more while Ingram is out. If he does not, he can go back to waivers.
